This PR is part of a stack (oldest at bottom):

* #44994
* __->__ #44993
* #44991
* #44480

## Motivation

Builds on #44480's focused FP8 fallback expert-ID repair. This PR extends the contract to wrapped and direct methods, routing formats, weight handling and transport payloads.

A mixed-precision or draft MoE layer can fall back to Triton while the requested backend remains FlashInfer or AITER. Dispatch and routing previously followed that request, so a local-ID kernel could receive global expert IDs or the wrong TopK format. Direct kernels and dormant fallback runners also mean that runner construction alone does not identify the execution contract.

## Modifications

- Quant methods expose their effective execution backend, including wrapped schemes, secondary AITER runners and direct kernels. FusedMoE records it before creating dispatch and binding each model router.
- Expert-ID mapping, TopK format, backend-specific post-load transforms, scaling, in-place behavior, DeepEP dtype and FlashInfer payloads consume the layer's contract. Missing implicit router bindings fail before invoking a kernel.
- Fallback layers preserve the model's DP all-gather/reduce-scatter layout using BF16 payloads. Ordinary block-FP8 post-load shuffling runs only for the actual AITER backend, including both FNUZ and non-FNUZ layouts.
- Backend binding is one-time and idempotent for the same contract; conflicting rebinding fails before changing router state. LLaDA2 consumes the authoritative layer backend, including the direct-kernel None case.
- The gfx1250 W4A8 internal router rejects unsupported expert sharding at startup.
- Muse Spark BF16/FP4 custom SP configs declare the direct execution backend; update the Kimi weekly experts fixture to model the same backend association.

Ordinary W13/W2 loaders explicitly zero every untouched tail after checkpoint shard selection. This preserves already-padded allocations when the requested TRTLLM runner falls back to Triton, including repeated loads.

Requested backend reads remain where they select a quant method, allocate compatible weight shapes, enforce startup compatibility or establish model-wide layout/default policy.

## Accuracy Tests

Current runner head: `1df050765ef3a9c247948475ca524118fa417d82`, stacked over #44480 and #44991. Exact combined stack `0177861c1117141b6e07d3c4c67b28898edd290c` passed 396 CPU tests plus 166 subtests across ten files; all 123 changed-file and ten test hashes matched before and after execution. Strict registration/suite validation, configured pre-commit and independent source review of the new repairs passed.

The new test uses real ModelOpt FP8 allocation and weight loading under the GPU loading policy on Torch CPU. Four padded configurations fail on poisoned tails before the repair; the aligned control passes. Afterward, TP1/TP2, global/presharded, gated/nongated and repeated loading match an independent unpadded expert reference and remain finite. This validates loading and dequantized CPU math; FP8 GPU-kernel execution was not rerun.

The Kimi weekly file failed before the fixture update (1 passed, 1 failed) and passed both existing tests afterward. The Muse Spark test constructs real BF16/FP4 experts and the real SP dispatcher, substituting the external workspace/communication boundary: both configs passed sentinel `num_experts` before and `-1` after. This proves the contract wiring, not a Muse Spark GPU crash or model numerical result. The migrated #44480 regression and five adjacent files passed 82 tests plus 20 subtests together; a detected test-state leak was repaired without weakening assertions.

The earlier hardware results below keep their named revisions. No final-head GPU, AMD/NPU, throughput or all-CI-green result is claimed by this restack.


The CI follow-up preserves weight-only Inkling helpers that never create a runner. Both BF16 restoration and optional SwiGLU interleaving now decline backend-specific work when the effective backend is None. A real InklingBatchDenseMLP regression loads, reloads and linearizes the expert weights through its actual loading mixin. The older DeepGEMM fixture now uses a serialized-FP8 configuration and the real method constructor. At production revision `573c93aa68f608deb79597314b1d3f1e96b2d190`, StandardDispatcher passed 13 tests plus 10 subtests and FP8 ownership passed 6 tests plus 6 subtests. All 7 DeepGEMM requantization tests passed with the corrected test file; its SHA-256 matches then-head `ba9f071c06c18ad594654ab4448cd9b114cf492c` exactly.

The binding/LLaDA2 follow-up passed source review and pre-commit. At `314f1a85190af5331eefa4a70a22eeb3983b5336`, StandardDispatcher passed 12 tests plus 10 subtests and ServerArgs passed 303 tests plus 135 subtests. After correcting only the LLaDA2 EP topology fixture, all 16 LLaDA2 tests plus 2 subtests passed at final head `97c954fdf334055dee221483622a5b8ae02c6e05`. The gfx94x numerical regression adapted from #41636 collects and skips correctly on non-ROCm hardware; its ROCm numerical execution remains unrun.

At `925dc371b069ecbb59037fc56d735cde4bbc45bc`, Linux CPU tests pass with GPUs hidden:

- `test_fp8_moe_runner_ownership.py`: 6 tests and 6 subtests, including byte/dtype/scale checks for both AITER shuffle guards.
- `test_standard_dispatcher.py`: 11 tests and 7 subtests, including real FusedMoE construction for FP8/BF16 fallbacks, unsupported AITER shapes, direct/dormant/wrapped methods and DP fallback payloads.
- `test_moe_runner_extensions.py`: 8 tests.

Existing HPC guard, shared-scaling, FlashInfer dispatcher, config-placement, W4AFP8 dtype and LoRA pool tests passed at `961d751716dcbbac6eed60832bf92da4bcc875fe`; baseline tests also passed before the refactor. Precommit and whole-diff whitespace checks pass.

On 4 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, a tiny Qwen3MoeForCausalLM at TP4/EP4 using an explicit MegaMoE runner request and the actual unquantized Triton fallback produced identical token IDs and a maximum generated-token logprob difference of 0.0 against baseline Triton for three prompts (24 generated tokens). This used candidate `961d751716dcbbac6eed60832bf92da4bcc875fe` and baseline `a3abea35609eeeff7e165486dd614963af211161`, with PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 and FlashInfer 0.7.1. DeepGEMM 0.2.2 was installed but was not exercised by this Triton smoke.

The final combined stack at `089abd45de22413e219942dad305f2183734845c` also passed the same synthetic BF16 Qwen3MoE smoke on 4 NVIDIA B300 GPUs, with TP4/EP4, a requested MegaMoE runner using the Triton fallback, reversed expert placement, and full decode CUDA graphs enabled together. Batch transitions 3 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 matched all 72 generated token IDs against the identity-placement baseline, with maximum generated-token logprob difference 0.0. A 48-token continuation remained finite and the server log confirmed graph replay. This is a routing regression smoke, not a task-level accuracy evaluation.

A real mixed-precision Qwen3MoE checkpoint also ran at final runner head `97c954fdf334055dee221483622a5b8ae02c6e05`: one block-FP8 expert layer and one BF16 expert layer, TP4/EP4 on 4 NVIDIA B300 GPUs. Under the CUTLASS request, all four ranks observed Triton for the FP8 layer and CUTLASS for the BF16 layer. The FP8 expert outputs for the first 14 real prefill rows matched the same-checkpoint Triton baseline bit-for-bit on every rank, with nonzero outputs on every rank. All 24 greedy token IDs matched; maximum generated-token logprob difference was 0.0039258003. BF16 expert outputs differed by at most 0.0001220703125 when using the different kernel. This is a reduced mixed-method execution test, not full-model accuracy validation.

The real `thinkingmachines/Inkling` CI checkpoint at revision `85b071f87d9bf5ff16a213a2d825faeed3af2cbf` also loaded successfully and generated 8 tokens with finite logprobs on one NVIDIA B300 GPU (TP1/EP1, eager execution), using production revision `573c93aa68f608deb79597314b1d3f1e96b2d190`. This checks startup and generation after the borrowed-loader repair; it does not validate the full hierarchical-cache suites.

The full model reproductions from #44291 and #40623, and ROCm/NPU/XPU/gfx1250 model execution, have not been run for this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not run; no throughput or latency improvement is claimed.

Refs #44291, #40623. Related #41636.
